Compounds 22a, 24a, sitagliptin, and MK-3102 with concentrations of 0 nM, 0.19 nM, 0.39 nM, 0.78 nM, 1.56 nM, 3.125 nM, 6.25 nM, 12.5 nM, and 25 nM were injected respectively for 480 s at a low speed of 30 μL/min. original_paragraph.Results and Discussion: Besides, we also performed surface plasmon resonance (SPR) experiments to evaluate the kinetic parameters of 22a binding to DPP-4 enzyme (Table 4 and Figure S7). As expected, compounds 22a and 5 are equipotent in terms of K_D values (2.38 nM vs 2.75 nM). Both compounds have quite long dissociation profile (k_off) compared with sitagliptin, which may be a favorable factor for long-lasting in vivo efficacy. Moreover, 22a associated faster than compound 5 (k_on (M−1 s−1): 1.44 × 10^6 vs 2.58 × 10^5) to DPP-4.
